changelog: Drawing tools now work in empty space, TradingView-style. Root cause, confirmed via Playwright before fixing: Lightweight Charts' coordinateToTime()/timeToCoordinate() only ever resolve a REAL candle's own time -- coordinateToTime(x) returns null for any x past the last loaded candle even though coordinateToLogical(x) (a continuous, bar-spacing-based scale) happily returns a valid logical index out there. Every placement/drag went through the null-returning path, so a click in blank space silently did nothing. Both directions (js/backtest-drawings.js: btXToTime, btTimeToX) now fall back to the logical-index scale, extrapolating a projected time from the nearest real edge candle using the timeframe's own fixed bar interval -- exact, not approximate, since this app's candles are always evenly spaced by timeframe.

A second, compounding bug in the same path: btSnapTimeToCandle() always force-snapped to the single nearest REAL candle with no distance cutoff at all, unconditionally -- which silently dragged any projected point straight back onto the last real candle, undoing the extrapolation above even after it was computed correctly. Rewritten to round to the nearest bar-interval boundary via the same logical-index math, instead of a nearest-candle search; behaviour for on-chart clicks is unchanged (same real candle chosen), but a point beyond either edge now rounds to the nearest projected bar instead of collapsing onto the edge candle.

js/chart.js's timeScale had no rightOffset configured (defaults to 0), so the last candle sat flush against the right edge -- there was no empty plot area to draw into at all, independent of the coordinate bug. Added rightOffset: 24, reserving real space to the right of the last candle the same way TradingView does.

Verified in-browser: placed a trend line, a position tool (dragged into blank space above and below the visible price range), and a fib retracement entirely in the empty space beyond the last candle; dragged an anchor further into that space; confirmed all three survive a pan and a zoom; then simulated real candles arriving in that space (the replay/timeframe-switch candle-array replacement) and confirmed every drawing's on-screen position recomputed correctly against the new real bars, with its stored projected time unchanged.

Settings panel rebuilt as a floating, draggable window (previously a fixed-position popover that clamped against a guessed ~300px height -- already wrong for the fib dialog's real size since v3.21.2, which is what 'opens pinned low, gets clipped, can't be moved' was describing). It now measures its own real rendered size before placing itself, always fits fully within the viewport with internal scrolling if the content is taller than the available space, is draggable by a new header (with a close button, closing on click same as the existing Escape handling), and remembers the position it was last dragged to (localStorage) across drawings and reloads. Before any drag has ever happened, it opens beside the clicked drawing with a gap rather than anchored on top of it, per the ticket -- a judgment call once the panel has been moved once, since 'remember its last position' and 'don't cover the tool by default' can't both govern the same open once a preference exists; documented inline.

Verified in-browser at a small (900x500) viewport, opening the panel at the worst-case bottom-right corner: fully within the viewport every time, header and close button present, body scrolls and every one of the fib dialog's settings (14 levels plus every toggle) is reachable, dragging by the header actually moves it, closing and reopening restores the exact dragged position, and both the close button and Escape hide it.

The v3.21.3 cache-busting ticket was already committed, tagged and pushed in the prior turn (commit 5d0e513, tag v3.21.3) -- confirmed against git log and the remote before starting this release rather than re-running it a second time.
release_notes: No schema changes in this release -- nothing to migrate. Per instruction, nothing was deployed as part of this turn.
